references.text: The parallel list of unclean birds in Leviticus that forbids the eagle, the vulture, and the sea eagle, with almost identical wording to Deuteronomy 14:12.

The complete list of unclean birds in Leviticus corresponding to the prohibitions in Deuteronomy 14:12-18, providing the full provisions of the Mosaic Law regarding which birds the Israelites were not to eat.
Job uses the eagle (nesher) as a metaphor for scavenging birds gathering around dead bodies, illustrating the symbolic meaning of this unclean bird.
Micah mentions the eagle (nesher) in connection with judgment and destruction, illustrating why this bird was considered unclean in Israelite tradition.
